label: no
controls_available: Full interaction uses edge turn arrows and direct tray-object drags onto scene geometry or another tray object.
autonomous_processes: None during active puzzle play: views, flags, inventory, lock state, and the replay transcript change only in response to agent input handlers.

After the final successful door action, the CSS vault-door transform transitions for 0.8 seconds; this is post-success presentation after the outcome is submitted, with no remaining outcome-affecting control opportunity.
grouped_control_modes: Visible scene-hotspot clicks for flipping, opening, collecting, revealing, or opening the door.
Full-mode drag from an inventory card to another inventory card for object combination.
Full-mode drag from an inventory card to a visible scene target for object use.
Door lock panel controls: opening a digit or colour ward, advancing digit wheels, choosing colour keys, and submitting the ward entry.
Background clicks and invalid drops record misses or misuses; they do not create an autonomous control mode.

clause_i.reason: No valid common real-time witness is available. Static seed-specific clues can make some action choices observation-dependent, but the source has no autonomous process whose visible evolution supplies that dependence; fixed topology and action order can otherwise be scheduled from I_t.

clause_ii.reason: No bounded recent window predicts a delayed change in this task. A screenshot-only solver uses static visible scene geometry and clues revealed by its own actions, while the configured observation window is 0 ms and nothing continues evolving between actions.

clause_iii.reason: Fails decisively: the browser model has no timer, requestAnimationFrame loop, physics, moving target, or changing lock during active play. navigate, sceneAction, performCombine, performUse, and submitWard update state synchronously inside input handlers; three-strike seizure is action-count based. The only CSS transition is the 0.8-second vault-door opening after successful terminal submission, so it cannot make an available outcome-affecting action strictly worse.

common_visible_process: None. The static room art and seed-generated clue geometry are fixed for the instance. The only autonomous-looking visual change is the post-terminal vault-door transition, which is not an active task opportunity and cannot witness clauses (i)-(iii).

pre_run.reason: There is no autonomous outcome phase: every puzzle-state transition needed for success is initiated by an agent click, turn, lock entry, or drag. The mathematical definition already fails clause (iii), so a pre-run threshold override is unnecessary.

source_evidence.claim: The exact level-3 parameters are six fixed views, digit/color/key wards, four digits, five colors, combined hook construction, no decoys, unmarked cues, no cross-view order, and three wrong entries; full mode is direct dragging with 0-ms observations and one frame.

Random digits, colors, view palettes, and target rectangles are generated once before play; the generator defines fixed view roles and static flag-gated scene targets, with no ongoing time or motion process.
Turns, scene discoveries, combinations, item uses, ward releases, and three-strike seizure are performed synchronously in response to input events.

Submission is a result fetch after the final action; drag handling records geometry/travel evidence but has no task-time mechanic, and rendering initializes a static model without timers or animation loops.
The only relevant transition is the 0.8-second vault-door transform after opening; the rest of the room and inventory styling is static, and the transition follows terminal success.

The grader replays an ordered event list synchronously, validates direct-manipulation geometry, and applies lock seizure from wrong-entry counts; it records no timestamps or autonomous state evolution.
The task verifier only loads the exported result and invokes the reliquary replay grader; it has no timing condition.
The reference UI solver proceeds through fixed turns, visible hotspots, drags, and lock submissions, then waits only for the final pass readout; it contains no timing or motion control.
The shared verifier helper only copies and parses /tmp/task_result.json, so the verification path adds no task-time behavior.
